input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 gives Customer a convenience right at the end of any calendar month on one month's notice, which meets the preferred notice standard, and IBM has no mid-term convenience right (Section 3.2 allows only 90 days' non-renewal at end of term, consistent with the fallback). The material failure is the exit cost: termination is conditioned on paying whatever early termination charges Attachment A or a Service Option Attachment specifies, with no cap, and there is no refund of prepaid charges (Section 3.5 accelerates all accrued payment obligations). An uncapped charge can economically negate the convenience right, failing the fallback limit of three months' fees. Redline caps the charge at three months' charges for the terminated Services and adds a pro-rata refund of prepaid charges; notice period and the absence of an IBM convenience right are left unchanged.

proposal.summary: Cap early termination charges at three months' charges and add pro-rata refund of prepaid charges on convenience termination
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have kept IBM's early termination charges but capped them at three months' charges for the terminated Services and added a pro-rata refund of prepaid charges, so our one-month convenience exit is not neutralised by an uncapped penalty. Our preferred position is convenience termination with no charge, and we are happy to discuss the cap level.

ops.newText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, provided that such charges will not, in the aggregate, exceed three (3) months' charges for the terminated Services. IBM will refund to Customer any charges prepaid for the period after the effective date of termination.
